title: API Fidelity PRD for Generation, Embeddings, and Reranking — Launch Rundown & Acceptance Matrix
creator: Ben Carter
description: Purpose: Define a concise behavioral and operational spec that guarantees fidelity of the hosted API across generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and reranking surfaces. This PRD focuses on exact behavior contracts, compatibility tolerances, and an operational launch rundown with an acceptance matrix to minimize customer regressions. It clarifies scope changes since the Q1 spec, captures trade-offs (latency vs. unit cost vs. determinism), and lists the rollout playbook for staged region + tier canary + automatic fallback.
acceptance_criteria: API contract: chat/completions endpoints must return stable field names and types for 99.99% of requests compared to the nominated v1 baseline; any intentional change requires a compatibility flag and migration notes.
Streaming parity: streaming behavior (chunk framing, delta tokens, finalization) must match SDK semantics; SDK e2e tests green in Node/Python for both streaming and chunked JSON outputs.

Embeddings consistency: embedding vectors for the canonical test corpus (10 documents) must have cosine similarity >= 0.995 to the validated model baseline across 3 consecutive runs after quantization profile selection.
Rerank determinism: given the same input and rerank model version, top-5 rank order must be stable in 99.5% of runs; documented nondeterminism window must be communicated in API docs.
Latency SLOs: p95 latency for single-request generation (no batching) must be <= 180ms for short prompts (<64 tokens) on dedicated tier, and fallback to a compatible model must keep p95 <= 400ms.
Observability: per-request token breakdown, model variant, and route must be emitted and visible in Console traces for all production traffic in the canary region.

Rollout safety: automated rollback trigger on quality regressions (delta in eval set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity) or error rate spike >2x baseline for 10 minutes must be implemented and tested in staging.
Security & compliance: audit logs for inference payloads and key usage enabled for Private customers; KMS integration validated with one enterprise pilot customer.
scope: Define behavioral contracts for: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank endpoints including streaming and structured outputs.
Specify backward-compatibility rules and a migration flagging mechanism for breaking changes.
Acceptance matrix tying API contract tests, perf benchmarks, and eval metric thresholds to release gates.
Staged rollout plan: region canary (us-west-2), tier canary (dedicated small pool), and global ramp with fallback policies.
Operational runbooks for rollback, degraded-mode routing, and customer communication templates.
out_of_scope: Model architecture changes and retraining (handled by Applied ML team) except where model variants are required for fallbacks.
Dedicated capacity pricing changes and billing product decisions.
Onboarding of new modality types (vision/multimodal) — deferred to H2 roadmap.
rollout_checklist: API contract finalized and reviewed by SDK & Docs teams.
E2E test suite: passing for Node, Python, and Go SDKs in staging with streaming and structured output scenarios.
Performance benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 recorded and compared against baseline; quantization recommendations applied where cost wins without exceeding acceptance thresholds.
Console observability: traces, per-token cost, and alerting configured; dashboards created and shared with SRE and Support.
Canary deployment: roll to us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 48 hours with active eval set monitoring.
Customer pilot: enable feature for 2 beta customers on Dedicated and collect feedback for 2 weeks.
Rollback automation: toggles validated in staging and runbook rehearsed with SRE.
Docs and changelog: migration guidance, compatibility table, and sample code snippets published before global ramp.
Post-launch monitoring: 7-day quality guard and dedicated channel for rapid incidents.
open_questions: Trade-off: Do we allow bounded semantic drift in embeddings when switching to a quantized variant? Proposed acceptance: require embedding similarity >=0.995 for canonical corpus — confirm with Applied ML.
Should function-calling semantics be covered in this PRD or in a separate Function Calling RFC? Engineering recommends a later RFC; PM prefers inclusion for parity.
Fallback policy granularity: per-model variant or per-route? Need ENG input on operation complexity and cost impact.
Do enterprise Private customers require explicit opt-in for automatic fallback to managed model variants? Legal/security to advise.
